323195.title: The ordered K-theory conjecture for finitely separated graph C*-algebras
323195.statement:
Let $(E,C)$ be a finitely separated graph. Let $(G(E,C),G(E,C)^+)$ be the Grothendieck group of $M(E,C)$, with positive cone

$$
G(E,C)^+=\iota(M(E,C)),
$$

where $\iota\colon M(E,C)\to G(E,C)$ is the canonical map, which need not be injective. The natural homomorphism is

$$
(G(E,C),G(E,C)^+)\to (K_0(C^*(E,C)),K_0(C^*(E,C))^+).
$$

**Ordered K-theory conjecture.** This homomorphism of partially pre-ordered abelian groups is an isomorphism.

The underlying group map $G(E,C)\to K_0(C^*(E,C))$ is known to be an isomorphism, so the conjecture concerns whether the order structure on $K_0(C^*(E,C))$ is exactly the one induced by $G(E,C)^+$.

precise_gaps: Need a positive K0 class outside the graph cone, or a full positive-cone surjectivity argument. No finite certificate route identified.

323253.title: Jonsson's 3-torsion conjecture for matching complexes
323253.statement:
Let $n\geq 1$ and write

$$
n=2k+1+3r,\qquad d=k-1+r.
$$

Thus the relevant reduced homology group is $\tilde{H}_{k-1+r}(\mathsf{M}_{2k+1+3r};\mathbb{Z})$. **Jonsson's 3-torsion conjecture.** The group contains elements of order $3$ if and only if $k\geq 0$ and $r\geq 2$, and it is an elementary nonvanishing $3$-group if and only if $0\leq k\leq r-2$. This strengthens the known sufficient conditions for 3-torsion and elementary 3-groups in the parameter range, while the asserted equivalences remain conjectural.

mathematical_attempts: Conjecture 1.6 is an iff assertion about both existence of order-three elements and elementary entire homology. Proposition 1.4 already covers r>=3 for existence and the nonvanishing 3-group range; proving only these is duplication.
precise_gaps: Unproved r=2 general existence and elementary exponent-three classification; cannot substitute mod-3 Betti numbers for integral torsion. Huge boundary matrices make unguided execution inappropriate.

323424.title: Even-degree homology conjecture for graph moduli spaces
323424.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a graph, and let $\mathscr{M}(\Gamma)$ denote its associated moduli space. For an odd integer $i$, write $H_i(\mathscr{M}(\Gamma))$ for its $i$-th homology group.

**Even-degree homology conjecture.** For any graph $\Gamma$ and every odd integer $i$,

$$
H_i(\mathscr{M}(\Gamma))=0.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the homology of $\mathscr{M}(\Gamma)$ is supported in even degrees. The paper proves the corresponding vanishing in the specific example discussed earlier, but states that it is not yet able to establish the assertion for general graphs.

323533.title: Generalized truncated Gauss identity for $J_{m,r}(n)$
323533.statement:
Let $m,n,k,r\geqslant 1$ with $r\leqslant m/2$. Define $J_{m,r}(n)$ by

$$
\sum_{n=0}^\infty J_{m,r}(n)q^n=\frac{1}{(q^{r},q^{m-r},q^m;q^m)_\infty}.
$$

**Generalized truncated Gauss conjecture.** There holds

$$
(-1)^{k-1}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(-1)^j\Bigl(J_{m,r}\bigl(n-j(mj+m-2r)/2\bigr)-J_{m,r}\bigl(n-(j+1)(mj+2r)/2\bigr)\Bigr)\geqslant 0,
$$

with strict inequality if $n\geqslant k(mk+m-2r)/2$.

This conjecture simultaneously generalizes inequalities for overpartitions, ordinary partitions, and partitions into distinct parts. The source notes that it is effectively identical with Problem 2 in the final version of a work of George E. Andrews and colleagues; no resolution is given here.

323592.title: Algebra grading conjecture for generalized uniform-poset algebras
323592.statement:
Fix distinct integers $s,t$, a finite set $\mathbb I\subseteq\mathbb Z\setminus\{s,t\}$, nonzero scalars $\gamma_i\in\mathbb F$ for $i\in\mathbb I$, and

$$
\phi(K)=\sum_{i\in\mathbb I}\gamma_iK^i.
$$

Let $\alpha_s,\alpha_t$ be central and let $S$ be the algebra with

$$
RL=\alpha_sK^s+\alpha_tK^t+\phi(K),
$$

$$
LR=\alpha_sq^{-2s}K^s+\alpha_tq^{-2t}K^t+\phi(q^{-2}K).
$$

**The generalized grading conjecture.** The corresponding algebra $S$ has a direct-sum algebra grading

$$
S=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb Z}S_n,
$$

where $S_0$ has basis $K^h\alpha_s^i\alpha_t^j$, $S_n$ has basis $R^nK^h\alpha_s^i\alpha_t^j$ for $n\geq1$, and $S_{-n}$ has basis $L^nK^h\alpha_s^i\alpha_t^j$ for $n\geq1$, in every case with $h\in\mathbb Z$ and $i,j\in\mathbb N$. The source gives no proof or resolution.

323732.title: Golumbic–Monma–Trotter conjecture on tolerance and cocomparability graphs
323732.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **tolerance graph** is a graph admitting a tolerance representation, and a **bounded tolerance graph** is a tolerance graph admitting a representation with no unbounded vertices. A **cocomparability graph** is a graph whose complement is a comparability graph.

**Golumbic–Monma–Trotter conjecture.** The intersection of cocomparability graphs with tolerance graphs is exactly the class of bounded tolerance graphs.

Every bounded tolerance graph is known to be both a tolerance graph and a cocomparability graph, so only the reverse inclusion is conjectural. The claim is known for complements of trees and complements of bipartite graphs, but remains open in general.

323748.title: The authors' characterization of radically solvable rigid graphs
323748.statement:
Let $G$ be a rigid graph. A graph is **quadratically solvable** if a generic framework can be solved using quadratic extensions, and **radically solvable** if a generic framework can be solved using radical extensions. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the recursively defined family of graphs constructed in the paper.

**The authors' rigid-graph characterization conjecture.** The following statements are equivalent:

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(a)} & G\text{ is quadratically solvable},\\
\text{(b)} & G\text{ is radically solvable},\\
\text{(c)} & G\in\mathcal{F}.
\end{array}
$$

The paper proves the corresponding statement for planar graphs. It explains that the conjecture is equivalent to the 3-connected conjecture above, so the unresolved issue is the removal of planarity.

precise_gaps: Need radical solvability of a non-globally-rigid three-connected generic framework, or the converse theorem in all graphs. Nongeneric rational-coordinate examples do not certify generic radical solvability.

323797.title: Block-repetition identities for alternating-sign-matrix numbers
323797.statement:
Let $A_n:=\alpha(n;1,2,\ldots,n)$, where $\alpha$ is the generalized monotone-triangle enumeration. Let $n\geq1$, let $i$ range over $0,\ldots,n$, and define

$$
W_{n,i}=\alpha(2n+1;i,2,\ldots,n+1,1,2,\ldots,n),\qquad i=1,\ldots,3n+2.
$$

**Block-repetition conjecture.** The identities

$$
A_n=\alpha(n+i;1,2,\ldots,i,1,2,\ldots,n),
$$

for $i=0,\ldots,n$, and

$$
A_n=(-1)^n\alpha(2n+1;1,2,\ldots,n+1,1,2,\ldots,n)
$$

should hold, and the numbers $W_{n,i}$ should satisfy

$$
W_{n,i}=W_{n,3n+3-i}.
$$

These identities were conjectured using mathematical computation, and the source presents bijective proofs as an open direction.

323802.title: Polynomial-ratio conjecture for repeated-entry generalized monotone triangles
323802.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be the generalized monotone-triangle enumeration, let $A_{n-1}:=\alpha(n-1;1,2,\ldots,n-1)$, and let $n\geq k\geq4$. **Polynomial-ratio conjecture.** There exist polynomials $p_k(n)$ and $q_k(n)$ satisfying

$$
\deg p_k-\deg q_k=k-3
$$

and

$$
\alpha(n+1;1,2,\ldots,k-3,k-1,k,k-1,k,\ldots,n)=\frac{p_k(n)}{q_k(n)}A_{n-1}.
$$

The source gives two lower-index computational examples before formulating this general conjecture; it supplies no proof or resolution.

323881.title: Type C and type D Chan–Robbins–Yuen volume conjecture
323881.statement:
Let $CRYC_{n+1}$ and $CRYD_{n+1}$ denote the type $C_{n+1}$ and type $D_{n+1}$ analogues of the Chan–Robbins–Yuen polytope $CRYA_n$. For a nonnegative integer $k$, let

$$
Cat(k)=\frac{1}{k+1}\binom{2k}{k}
$$

be the $k$th Catalan number. **Type C and type D Chan–Robbins–Yuen volume conjecture.** The normalized volumes satisfy

$$
\operatorname{vol}(CRYC_{n+1})=2^{(n-1)^2+n}\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}Cat(k),
$$

$$
\operatorname{vol}(CRYD_{n+1})=2^{(n-1)^2}\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}Cat(k).
$$

These polytopes are introduced as analogues of $CRYA_n$; the paper proves their vertex counts, but the displayed volume formulas are conjectural and no resolution is given.

323936.title: Ground-state domination conjecture for the Friedrichs spectrum
323936.statement:
Let $P$ be a symmetric critical operator in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$, and let $\phi_0$ be a ground state of $P$. For $\lambda>0$, let $\phi_\lambda$ solve

$$
(P-\lambda)u=0
$$

in $\Omega$ and suppose that there is a constant $C>0$ such that

$$
|\phi_\lambda(x)|\leq C\phi_0(x) \qquad \forall x\in\Omega.
$$

**Ground-state domination conjecture.** Then $\lambda$ belongs to the spectrum of the Friedrichs extension of $P$ on $L^2(\Omega,\mathrm{d}x)$. This conjecture links pointwise domination by a ground state to spectral inclusion for the Friedrichs extension; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

323940.title: Cubic or 3-connected hardness conjecture for Pirates and Treasure
323940.statement: Let $G$ be the graph input to the Pirates and Treasure game. A graph is **cubic** if every vertex has degree $3$, and **3-connected** if deleting fewer than three vertices does not disconnect it. **Cubic or 3-connected hardness conjecture.** Pirates and Treasure is NP-hard if $G$ is either cubic or 3-connected. This would extend the established NP-hardness results for planar and grid graphs to graph classes for which the path-adding reduction does not preserve the required structure; the source gives no resolution.

324169.title: Aluffi's Euler characteristic conjecture for graph hypersurface complements
324169.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite graph with graph hypersurface $X_\Gamma\subset\mathbb P^{n-1}$, and write $Y_\Gamma=\mathbb P^{n-1}\smallsetminus X_\Gamma$ for its projective hypersurface complement. **Aluffi's conjecture.** The Euler characteristic satisfies

$$
\chi(Y_\Gamma)\in\{0,1,-1\}.
$$

This conjecture had been confirmed by computer calculations for many sufficiently small graphs and for some other classes of graphs. If true, it would imply that the Euler characteristics of the graph hypersurfaces $X_\Gamma$ are always non-negative.

324193.title: Gessel's conjecture on the two-sided Eulerian polynomial
324193.statement:
Let $A_n(s,t)$ denote the two-sided Eulerian polynomial. For $n\geq 1$, the polynomial is considered in the basis

$$
(st)^i(s+t)^j(1+st)^{n+1-j-2i},
$$

with indices satisfying $0\leq i-1$, $j$, and $j+2i\leq n+1$. **Gessel's conjecture.** There exist nonnegative integers $\gamma_{n,i,j}$ such that

$$
A_n(s,t)=\sum_{i,j}\gamma_{n,i,j}(st)^i(s+t)^j(1+st)^{n+1-j-2i}.
$$

The conjecture asserts nonnegativity of the coefficients in the basis determined by the symmetries of the two-sided Eulerian polynomial. The source gives no resolution status, so it remains open here.

\overline{\mathcal{C}}(k,d)=2d\quad\text{if }2d-\sqrt{d/2}\leq k\leq 2d-2.

324213.title: The tree domination-game pair conjecture
324213.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, and let $\gamma_g(T)$ and $\gamma_g'(T)$ denote the Dominator-start and Staller-start game domination numbers, respectively. A pair $(r,s)$ is **realizable by a tree** if there is a tree $T$ with $(\gamma_g(T),\gamma_g'(T))=(r,s)$.

**Tree domination-game pair conjecture.** No pair of the form $(k,k-1)$ can be realized by a tree.

The paper proves that $(3,2)$ and $(4,3)$ are not realizable and establishes realizability for the other discussed families, while the general nonrealizability of $(k,k-1)$ remains conjectural.

324401.title: NP-completeness of higher graph powers of girth $2k+1$
324401.statement: Let $k$ and $r$ be positive integers. The problem \textsc{$k^{th}$Power of a Graph With Girth $r$} asks, given a graph $G$, whether there exists a graph $H$ of girth $r$ such that $G=H^k$. **Higher-power girth conjecture.** The problem \textsc{$k^{th}$Power of a Graph With Girth $r$} for $r=2k+1$ is NP-complete. The conjecture proposes the missing NP-complete case in a complete girth-parametrized complexity dichotomy for higher graph-root finding; related results establish NP-completeness when $r=k$ and a polynomial-time algorithm for finding all $k^{th}$ roots of girth $2k+3$.

precise_gaps: Need a full parameter-uniform hardness reduction preserving required root girth. Source k=2 square-root result does not establish all powers.

324466.title: Non-embeddability conjecture for finite thick buildings
324466.statement: A **finite thick building** is a finite building in which every panel is contained in at least three chambers, and its dimension is denoted by $d$. **Non-embeddability conjecture.** No $d$-dimensional finite thick building embeds into $\mathbb{R}^{2d}$. This conjecture is motivated by the complex structure of finite thick buildings; the paper confirms it for several large classes of buildings, while the general case remains open.

324469.title: The finite-group formulation of the Lonely Runner Conjecture
324469.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $S\subset\mathbb{N}$ have size $k$, and for a natural number $n$ let $\mathbb{Z}_n$ denote the cyclic group of order $n$. For an integer $m$, set

$$
B=\pm\{0,1,\ldots,m\},\qquad m=\left\lceil\frac{n}{k+1}\right\rceil-1.
$$

**The finite-group formulation.** There exist a natural number $n$ and an element $x\in\mathbb{Z}_n$ such that

$$
xS\cap B=\varnothing.
$$

This is presented as an equivalent formulation of the Lonely Runner Conjecture in terms of dilates in cyclic groups. The general conjecture remains open.
324469.review_depth: Primary finite-group formulation inspected; famous hard topic parked without modulus sweeps.
mathematical_attempts: The finite cyclic formulation has an existential n and x for every positive-velocity set S. It is the general Lonely Runner conjecture, not a fixed finite problem. A failure for one modulus is not a counterexample.
precise_gaps: Need one S for which every modulus fails, or a full construction for arbitrary positive S. Allowing velocity0 merely exploits a natural-number convention and carries no credit.
